answer: Completed the full B3 task. A stochastic De Young–Keizer/Li-Rinzel IP3R simulation (3 subunits × 8 states, s=4k+2j+i, open iff all three subunits in s=3) was propagated directly with a 1 ms binomial τ-leap over the (N,3) subunit array, coupled by RK4 to the two-compartment Ca balance (Li–Rinzel c1 factor, flux ∝ open fraction, Hill-2 pump). All 60 grid points (6 IP3 × 5 N × 2 replicates, 20 s burn-in + 120 s observation, fixed seeds) ran in ~22 s wall on 16 processes. Deliverables in cwd: simulate.py (matplotlib-Agg primary, documented pure-Python PNG fallback), ca_traces.npz (30 keys ip3{i}_N{j}, all (2,1200) float64, replicates distinct), summary_stats.json (exactly the 7 required keys), calcium_summary.png (1400×1000, 4 panels, verified rendered). Headline results: period_vs_ip3 = [null, null, 31.7, 16.7, 13.0, 11.3 s] at N=800 (two lowest ligand levels are sub-threshold, honestly reported as null); cv_isi_vs_N = [0.416, 0.474, 0.368, 0.200, 0.176] at the recorded low-ligand index cr_ip3_idx_used = 3 (0.3886 µM; idx 0–2 were degenerate — see anomalies); p_open_vs_ip3 = [0.0119, 0.0212, 0.0268, 0.0436, 0.0529, 0.0644], monotonically increasing and matching the quasi-static mean-field p3³ within 2–6% at every level; conservation_error_max = 7.1e-14 (machine precision, as expected for an RK4-preserved linear invariant). Step-size sensitivity checked at 1 ms vs 0.5 ms (period/f_open differences within run-to-run stochastic variation).
